quote: Unsere Enkel werden uns auslachen, dass wir noch immer jeden Abend haben unsere Uhr müssen aufziehen, da doch wegen der Ungiltigkeit des 2ten Hauptsatzes perpetuum mobile 2ter Art längst technisch gefunden worden ist.
english: Our grandchildren will laugh at us that we still had to wind our clocks every evening, since, owing to the invalidity of the second law, a perpetual motion machine of the second kind will long since have been found technically.
topic: Notes on using a mean-free-path-type method to solve an integral equation, on the role of experiment and the axiomatic method in mathematics versus physics, a speculative remark on the second law of thermodynamics and perpetual motion of the second kind, and the start of a statistical (Boltzmann-type) maximization for the distribution of molecular energies.

triage.modern_statement: This is not a mathematical research question. It is a speculative prediction about physics and technology: that the second law of thermodynamics is not strictly valid (it holds only statistically), and that a perpetual motion machine of the second kind will therefore one day be built. Such a machine would be a cyclic device that turns heat from a single reservoir into macroscopic work, which the Kelvin–Planck statement forbids. Put in modern terms, the question is whether statistical fluctuations or a Maxwell's-demon-type mechanism can be used to beat the second law systematically and on a macroscopic scale.
triage.answered_by: There was no single resolution. The physics community has worked through it via the Maxwell's-demon line: Szilard (1929), then Landauer and Bennett (Landauer's principle, Bennett's analysis around 1982), who concluded that a demon cannot violate the second law because it produces entropy. This conclusion is still debated on foundational grounds, for example Earman–Norton and the 'circularity' critique. Fluctuation theorems (Evans–Searles; Wang, Sevick, Mittag, Searles and Evans, PRL 89, 050601, 2002) showed experimentally that the second law is broken briefly in small systems over short times. No macroscopic perpetual motion machine of the second kind has been built, and Hilbert's prediction has not come true. The note is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems. It does connect loosely to the 6th problem, the axiomatization of physics and probability and Boltzmann's kinetic theory, where Deng, Hani and Ma reported in 2025 a derivation of the fluid equations via Boltzmann's equation.

evidence.claim: Bennett, like Szilard (1929), concluded that a Maxwellian demon cannot violate the second law because entropy is created, though for different reasons. Others, including Norton, have challenged this resolution.
The Landauer/Bennett resolution of Maxwell's demon has been criticized as circular, because Landauer's principle was derived on the assumption that the second law holds.

Wang et al. (2002) experimentally demonstrated the fluctuation theorem, which predicts measurable violations of the second law for small systems over short time scales. They used a colloidal particle held in an optical trap.
The second law is statistical: it follows from the fact that individual molecular motions are neither observed nor controlled.

Related to Hilbert's 6th problem: in 2025 Deng, Hani and Ma reported a rigorous derivation of the Euler and Navier–Stokes equations from Newtonian particle dynamics via Boltzmann's kinetic theory. Critics argue that the 6th problem is still open in its full generality.

triage.why: The remark is a deliberately provocative physical and technological prophecy, not a mathematical statement that could be proved. Nothing in the sources shows a macroscopic perpetual motion machine of the second kind has been built. Mainstream physics holds the second law as statistically valid for macroscopic systems: small, short-lived violations are confirmed only at the scale of fluctuations, and the Maxwell's-demon analyses (Szilard, Landauer, Bennett) argue that the law cannot be exploited systematically. My search found nothing that links this specific diary note to any later literature. The underlying topics are still active research: stochastic thermodynamics, the thermodynamics of information and Maxwell's demon, and the foundations of statistical mechanics. 'Active today' refers to those topics, not to any work building on Hilbert's prediction. Confidence is medium for three reasons: the verdict category is a judgment call (it is a physics conjecture, not mathematics), the foundations of the demon resolution are still argued over, and one of my searches (the Kelvin–Planck statement) failed, so no source is cited for that definition.
